notes.title: First Steam Playtest Coming to an End
notes.notes: [p]Hello folks![/p][p][/p][p]As the first Steam Playtest is wrapping up, I just wanted to say a big thanks to everyone for playtesting this very early version of the game. I have a couple things to announce, but first, I just wanted to say a [u]huge[/u] thank you to everyone who helped me track down bugs, come up with some great new ideas, and just helped me make the game better in general. [/p][p][/p][list][*][p]The playtest will be closing on [b]July 17, 2025[/b]. The game is moving into the next stage of development, so sadly, we need to leave the playtest behind. I'm still optimistic that your skill tree progress can saved, but it's hard to know in such an early build of the game. You lovely folks rated this game 4.2/5 on an average of over 50 form submissions, so although I know this game has a long way to go, this really helps me see that you enjoyed it. It brings me a lot of joy to know that people actually played this game and had a good time![/p][/*][*][p]The game has an official website now with some nice visual and audio interaction: [url="https://bushcraftsurvivalgame.com/"]https://bushcraftsurvivalgame.com/[/url][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]What can you do in the mean time?[/h2][p]Keep playing the playtest until it closes if you'd like![/p][p]Feedback and suggestions are huge for how I'm developing this game, so I want to make sure you feel heard. [/p][p][/p][p][b]In addition, make sure you Wishlist the game on Steam if you haven't already (PS. tell your friends about it too!). As many of you know, wishlisting the game is the biggest way you can support small indie developers.[/b] [/p]

notes.title: Free Build Mode is here! Get creative with your shelters
notes.notes:
[p]Hey everyone![/p][p]One of our posts recently blew up and an extremely common thing I heard is that players wanted to be able to use resources however they want.[/p][p]"I would play the hell out this [b]IF[/b] the large amount of grinding for supplies was followed up by as much freedom as possible with how I used them. If I make a lean-too let me do any angle or size I want. If I want a fire let me make it as big of a bon fire I can make. If I can dig let me dig a whole man made lake. Etc."
[/p][p]Well, I have listened to this feedback. The newest iteration of the Bushcraft Survival Playtest now uses a "free building mode", meaning you can basically do whatever you want with logs, boughs, and moss to build shelters.[/p][p][/p][p]Also [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ZvoyenHqc0"]check out the new How to Series on YouTube[/url], showing you how to make different shelters.[/p][p][/p][p]I won't say we can dig a whole man made lake YET, but we are getting there. The new open building system allows you to:[/p][list][*][p]Build lean-tos between any trees, in any configuration[/p][/*][*][p]You can attach logs between any of these three objects: trees, logs, or the ground. It creates a pretty huge number of combinations[/p][/*][*][p]You can build up into the sky. There's nothing stopping you! You'll just also have to build yourself a ramp to get up there[/p][/*][*][p]You can dig into the snow and lay logs, boughs, and moss across the top.[/p][/*][*][p]Build bonfires as large as you want![/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45603517/5105eb62b919eba124bd8ee01c8ad0d65a5bdfaf.png"][/img][/p][p]In a future update I hope to introduce "burning" as a general thing that can happen to anything in the game.[/p]

notes.title: Run Wild: Autorun is here! + Shorter Tutorial
notes.notes: [p]Hello Bushcrafters![/p][p]I got a ton of playtesting and feedback from the XP Games Summit this June in Toronto, so I am starting to roll out some of these updates.[/p][p]To summarize what players were saying:[/p][list][*][p]The tutorial was too long, and broken in some cases[/p][/*][*][p]Overwhelming amount of information, trying to figure out which tools to pick from the very first game load[/p][/*][*][p]Autorun! Makes total sense to me. I want to encourage people to explore the world, and make it easy for them to eat a snack while doing it[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Other patch notes for this build:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Tutorial has been reworked to be shorter, and more clear[/p][/*][*][p]UI icons added for interacting with objects such as trees, logs, firewood, moss, tinder, branches[/p][/*][*][p]Autorun has been added (thanks for the suggestion Kimi!)[/p][/*][*][p]Option when the game is first loaded to run the Survival tutorial in "challenge" mode, where stats such as temperature, hydration, etc. are still affected[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: BENEATH THE ICE: Death and Dinner
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]I have been very hard at work on the [b]Ice Fishing Update[/b] for Bushcraft Survival. I'm really happy about this update as the fishing mechanic brings together lots of pieces of the game:[/p][list][*][p]Falling through the ice. You now have a real reason to go out on the ice, but be careful. Too far and you'll fall in (hint... the rarest fish will be caught closer to the edge)[/p][/*][*][p]Food preparation and cooking mechanics[/p][/*][*][p]Ice Safety Picks - a tool you can use to haul yourself out of the frozen depths*[/p][/*][*][p]Raw fish fillets attracting wildlife*[/p][/*][/list][p]*these mechanics will be coming out in the next patch. For now I'm hoping people can jump in the game and let me know if they can get far enough into the experience to try ice fishing. Please let me know how it goes![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45603517/d0a3f28c63ffdfbc78756a9b0080e99f98289664.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Steam Achievements[/b] and a [b]Fishing Journal[/b] will be coming soon![/p][p][/p][h1]What's Next?[/h1][p]In addition, I've put together this [b]Road Map[/b] to let you all know where the game is headed.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45603517/19eef4892abf84b21848f2d2ab86bbb2aa788d1c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The playtest will be live for another month or so. [url="https://discord.gg/UyefbSJ3Hf"]Jump in the Discord[/url] and let me know how it was![/p][p][/p][p][b]Other patch notes for this build:[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Patch Notes June 11, 2025[/p][p]RELEASE: BETA[/p][p]VERSION: 0.1.5[/p][p]- Ice fishing added. This includes "drowning" mechanic (falling through the ice), and cooking. Read full community post here[/p][p]- Gamepad analog stick sensitivity increased[/p][p]- Gamepad vibration added. This can be turned off in Settings[/p][p]- Bug fix where terrain was changing the visuals, but the actual physics collision was not updating when digging into the terrain[/p][p]- Game actions reworked for pot and other single-use tools. Before you would have seen a green sphere showing where to use it, but now you just get the green dot[/p]

notes.title: v0.1.4 Patch
notes.notes: [p]Patch Notes June 6, 2025[/p][p]RELEASE: BETA[/p][p]VERSION: 0.1.4[/p][p]- Terrain system now uses Godot's RenderingServer API. This should give better multi-threaded performance[/p][p]- Terrain physics system upgraded, now using PhysicsServer API[/p][p]- Tree branch visuals slightly upgraded with some beveling, and fixed UV mapping[/p][p]- Tree branches now bend and move slightly as you move through dense forest. This should be a big improvement on controller support[/p][p]- Various UI upgrades, including UI tooltips and improved tutorial messages[/p]

notes.title: v0.1.3 Patch
notes.notes:
Patch Notes May 28, 2025
RELEASE: BETA
VERSION: 0.1.3

- Added hatchet game icon in taskbar
- Adjusted energy stat mechanic. The energy decrease is now non-linear and slows down once you fall below 10%. This reflects more real world scenarios, where you can go a long time without eating
- Adjusted HP stat mechanic for energy. Once energy is below the critical threshold (5% currently) you start to lose HP. Basically, you can die from starvation now
- Controller support added, with full keyboard mappings. There are two mapping slots provided for each action
- Tutorial improved, fire mechanic graphic made more clear
- Tutorial support for controllers, icons added to give more visual clarity
- Inventory bug fixed with picking up large logs
- "Place Bough" menu item renamed to "Green Bough" to be consistent with other items ("Place" doesn't appear anywhere else)

notes.title: BUSHCRAFT SURVIVAL Playtest is Open!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45603517/488574294603de7fe79b307fa99b6be0eefac2ea.png[/img]

Hi everyone!

I have been working on Bushcraft Survival for about 6 months and I have something playable that I’d love for you to test out and let me know what you think!

Bushcraft Survival is a hardcore survival game that - as the name implies - focuses on bushcrafting tools and skills, set in Canada's northern, frozen climate. Similar to The Long Dark, except you choose your loadout, manage your equipment, loot cabins to find new tools, and upgrade them through a skill tree XP system. The game is fully procedural in Survival mode, with a Story mode coming next year that will have hand crafted environments and landmarks.

One of the subtle things that makes this game different is that you are simulating the life of someone who goes out into the bush by choice. It’s not a reenactment of a plane crash or a zombie apocalypse.

If you’ve ever watched The Outdoor Boys on YouTube, or the show Alone, it’s a lot like that - you fill up your backpack with the essentials, head out to the bush and just survive. Ice fishing, trapping, and bushcraft shelter building are all skills that you will need to develop to survive. Things can, and will go wrong, so be prepared for that!

The Playtest is available on [b]Windows[/b] and [b]Linux[/b]

The graphics and UI aren’t super pretty at this stage - I’ll warn you about that. This game is all about the mechanics. I’m really trying to generate the feeling of what it’s like to be in the vice grip of nature. Getting over that hump and being able to survive is really rewarding.

[h2]What am I looking for from Survival gaming players?[/h2]

[list]
[*] Does the game run on your PC/laptop? I didn't get a ton of time to test on different setups. If not, could you report back when it crashed or if it didn't run at all
[*] What mechanics would you like to see developed next? There's a whole host of mechanics that I plan to develop, but would like to hear from you what's most important, or what order you'd like to see them develeoped
[/list]

There's a form linked on the title screen of the game that has an option for [b]Bug Reporting[/b] or [b]General Feedback[/b]. You can read more about the planned mechanics in General Feedback
